description: Measures how fast its input is changing and puts out the angle of that slope, -90 to 90 degrees scaled onto -10V to 10V, with the absolute value and the two halves out separately

params.text: Sets the frequency the slope is measured against, a fraction of a hertz up to 16Hz; it is also the sensitivity, since a higher setting makes the same change read as a steeper angle
Averages the input over up to 1 second before the slope is worked out, which takes the jitter out of a hand-moved controller

inputs.text: The signal whose rate of change is measured

outputs.text: The angle of the slope, 10V for a vertical rise, -10V for a vertical fall and 0V where the input is flat
The angle of the slope with the sign taken off, 0V where the input is flat and 10V for a vertical move either way
The angle of the slope while the input is rising, and 0V while it is falling or flat
The angle of the slope while the input is falling, put out as a positive voltage, and 0V while it is rising or flat

notes: the slope is measured once every two cycles of the FREQ setting rather than every sample, up to a limit of 1024 samples between measurements, so a low setting gives a coarser reading
every jack is monophonic, whatever is patched in
